fields.title: Knowledge that isn't written down is lost by the company
fields.keyTakeaway: An experiment result lives for three weeks in a participant's head and disappears with them. A short learning card — what was tested, what was obtained, what we now consider true — pays off on the very first repeat.
fields.checkQuestion: The team proposes testing an idea that was already tested a year ago. How will you find out?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key question of the node: **what new thing did we learn?**
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer the question.** A year later, a new product manager arrives and proposes exactly what didn't work. Nobody can confirm or refute it — they only remember that "there was something like that."
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: Half a page, written immediately after the experiment
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **What was assumed** — the entire hypothesis, with "because."
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **What was done** — on whom, how many, for how long.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **What was obtained** — numbers, including guardrail metrics.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **What we now consider true** — conclusion in one phrase. This is the only part that people will read.
fields.blocks/2/items/4: **What this doesn't prove** — boundaries of the conclusion. Saves you from applying the result where it doesn't work.
fields.blocks/3/text:
Assumed: personalized recommendations on the home screen will increase the number of books started because people find it hard to choose.
Done: 20% of the audience, three weeks.
Obtained: started books +0.4% (insignificant), finished books −2%.
Consider true: the problem is not choosing a book, but dropping the one already started.
Does not prove: that recommendations are useless altogether — we tested them only on the home screen and only for active users.

A year later, this idea was proposed again. The card was found in a minute, and the conversation took ten minutes instead of six weeks of development.
fields.blocks/3/title: Vetka, a card that saved six weeks
fields.blocks/4/text: "The test showed no effect" is not knowledge. Knowledge is "people don't choose because they drop what they started." The former closes the topic; the latter opens the next one.
fields.blocks/4/title: The conclusion "it didn't work" without a reason is useless
fields.blocks/5/text: **Where it lives.** The format doesn't matter: a wiki page, a table, a channel. Two things matter — a single place and the habit of looking there before proposing.
fields.blocks/6/text: The knowledge base gets outdated: the audience changes, the product changes. A two-year-old conclusion is a reason not to repeat blindly, not a ban on testing again with a new rationale.
